result.title: Segmentation of Moving Objects During Camera Motion Using the OWL Function
result.summary: We present a principled, analytical framework for segmenting multiple independently moving rigid objects during single camera motion, built directly upon the OWL perception function. OWL encodes two fundamental visual motion cues, perceived looming $L$ and perceived rotation $ω$, into a single closed-form representation of relative 3D structure. A key consequence of this structure is that the unit direction of relative translation $\hat{t}$ is analytically recoverable per image point from $L$ and $ω$ alone. All points belonging to a non-rotating rigid body share the same $\hat{t}$, whereas points on different rigid bodies generally yield distinct values. This furnishes a natural segmentation criterion: clustering per-point $\hat{t}$ estimates partitions the visible scene into independently moving rigid bodies. Building on the 2D complex form of OWL, we derive the framework in 3D using quaternions, for a single moving camera. The approach is parallel, camera rotation-invariant, and requires no training data, no depth information, and no semantic priors.

AI.brief_summary: 提出基于 OWL 感知函数的解析框架，把 looming 与旋转两个运动线索编码为相对三维结构的闭式表示，并可从每个图像点解析恢复相对平移方向，据此聚类分割相机运动下多个独立运动的刚体。
AI.relevance_reason: 其逐点解析、旋转不变的运动量及按该量聚类划分场景，可能为核查 VLM 内部状态是否保留几何与运动证据提供无训练的对照组，但与 latent 推理的生成、训练和监督机制无直接联系，需较多核查。
